Method of Attack: Information-stealing trojan that collects passwords and optionally drops other malware
Attack Vector: Purchased servers from web hosting companies used as C&C servers
Hacked servers used as C&C servers
Use of domain names registered via domain registrars (notably Namecheap) to host botnet controllers
Botnet controllers communicating with infected devices
Indicators of Compromise: IP addresses of C&C servers (over 9,500 new in 2017)
Domain names used for C&C servers (over 50,000 new domains in 2017)
Namecheap domains accounting for 25% of all C&C server domains
Hosting providers OVH and Amazon hosting most botnet controller IPs
Spamhaus Botnet Controller List (BCL) and Domain Block List (DBL)
